title: Leopard seal chapter 1: The charge
sources: National Geographic, 'How a Leopard Seal Fed Me Penguins' (Paul Nicklen, 11 Mar 2014): nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/140311-paul-nicklen-leopard-seal-photographer-viral : 2006 National Geographic assignment, female seal, head bigger than a grizzly bear's, took camera and head in her mouth, brought penguins alive then dead, four days, 'useless predator in her ocean'.

Natural History Museum London, 'Are leopard seals dangerous?': nhm.ac.uk/discover/are-leopard-seals-dangerous.html : up to 3.5 m and 500 kg, 2006 Nicklen encounter with worn-out dead penguins, possibly trying to teach him to hunt, Kirsty Brown 2003, ice edge, keep your distance.

Down To Earth / The Conversation (Hocking, Evans, Robbins), 'Buffet buddies' (downtoearth.org.in) and Cosmos 'Fierce leopard seals can be unexpected buffet buddies' (cosmosmagazine.com): Polar Biology 2019, South Georgia, Our Planet drone footage, up to 36 seals, taking turns on a king penguin, 'an offer to cooperate' reading of the Nicklen encounter.

Muir, Barnes and Reid 2006, 'Interactions between humans and leopard seals', Antarctic Science (cambridge.org/core/product/BAF5CBB6EF2469E7058BAEC09AB8B5A2): about 30 years of encounters, mostly curious, ice edge strongest, attacks rare, Brown's seal not seen beforehand, seals can act as predators toward humans.

National Geographic News, 'Leopard Seal Kills Scientist in Antarctica' (Aug 2003) and Discover Wildlife 'Leopard seal guide': Kirsty Brown, British Antarctic Survey, snorkelling near Rothera, July 2003, thought to be the first recorded human fatality from a leopard seal.

BMC Ecology 2020 (doi 10.1186/s12898-020-00300-y) on leopard seal spring diet: krill 32 to 38 percent, notothen fish 32 to 37 percent, penguin 24 to 27 percent. Frontiers in Marine Science 2022 (10.3389/fmars.2022.976019): adults and sizes, females about 50 percent larger than males.

lines.text: What would you do if a huge leopard seal swam straight at you with its mouth wide open?

lines.text: Then she did something he never expected. She took his camera into her mouth, and then his head.

lines.text: What came next made even less sense. Over the next four days, she started bringing him penguins.

lines.text: Why would a top predator of the Antarctic try to feed a human?

lines.text: That is the question for this whole video, and I will give you the honest answer at the end, including the part where nobody is sure.
